mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a quarter signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative shift during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth rate by more than 1% over the previous quarter indicates strengthening economic demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive demand signal, or 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive shift during strong GDP growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market improvement signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive shift during tightening labor market periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over the previous quarter signals a strengthening supply side, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as production capacity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive supply signal, or 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive shift during strong industrial production growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over the previous quarter indicates strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive housing demand signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive shift during strong housing starts growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where the current level of the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average predicts the direction of S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with higher rates relative to the average leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above its 12-month average, or 5-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative shift when FEDFUNDS is above its average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each over the previous three months signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the robust labor market signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive shift during periods of strong labor market indicators (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous quarter, during a period of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), signals a demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the demand contraction signal, or 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative shift during periods of declining consumption with high inflation (t-test p > 0.05).
